To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we introduce an incentive compatible auction design approach that is based on a time-independent Lagragian, which allows for a single metric to assess auction performance and avoids an expensive hyper-parameter sweep,  (2) we propose a neural architecture that amortizes the inner maximization loop of previous work, and

1) the introduction of the time-independent Lagrangians leads to a single metric that can be used to compare two auction mechanisms; 2) amortizing the inner maximization loop leads to improved auction mechanisms; 3) these two improvements combined allow us to formulate the problem of auction design as a two-player zero-sum game with stationary utility function.

(i) a time-independent Lagrangean is an effective way to circumvent hyper-parameter search in Auction Learning, (ii) a second neural network can be used to amortize the inner loop of the optimization procedure in Auction Learning, and (iii) Auction Learning can be formulated as a two-player zero-sum game with stationary utilities.
